newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin will keep seat in French assembly - poll.
newsitem.headline: Jospin will keep seat in French assembly - poll.

text.p: Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin has a strong lead over 15 challengers in France's May 25-June 1 parliamentary election and appears likely to regain the National Assembly seat he lost in 1993, a poll said on Monday.
The CSA poll for the daily Le Parisien newspaper found Jospin would be forced into a runoff if the election were held today but would emerge victorious in the second-round ballot.

It found Jospin with 39 percent of the vote to 24 percent for Marie-Denise Xerri, the candidate of the centre-right government, in the first round. The holder of the seat, Jean-Pierre Bastiani, another rightist, is not seeking re-election.
In the run-off, Jospin would take 59 percent of the vote to 41 percent for Xerri, the poll found.
The finding was based on interviews conducted on Sunday with 603 registered voters in Jospin's constituency in the Haute Garonne in southwestern France.
Jospin's Socialists are battling to oust the centre-right government in the election but the latest polls show the current majority remaining in power.
